item.title: Five Economists Vie for Croat Central Bank’s Vice Governor Posts
item.description: A Croatian parliamentary board chose five nominees endorsed by different parties to fill three vice governor positions at the central bank, according to people familiar with the matter.

item.title: Citigroup’s Manthey Double-Downgrades ‘Less Appealing’ UK Stocks
item.description: The UK stock market is defensive and tilted to commodities, making it less appealing as geopolitical tensions abate, according to Citigroup Inc. strategists.

item.title: European Stocks Drop After US-Iran Strikes, Oil Lifts Energy
item.description: European stocks fell as oil prices rose after the US and Iran exchanged fresh strikes overnight, with investors also focusing on the start of the earnings season.

item.title: Morgan Stanley’s Wilson Sees Profit Boost for Stocks Beyond Tech
item.description: US stocks beyond the technology giants are poised to report strong earnings this season, broadening the equity rally, according to Morgan Stanley strategists.

item.title: Africa’s Raxio to Enter Tanzania With $380 Million Funding Push
item.description: Africa-focused data-center firm Raxio Group plans to enter Tanzania as it increases its funding pool to $380 million, Chief Executive Officer Robert Mullins said.

item.title: South Korea to Tap Record AI Tax Windfall to Fund Future Growth
item.description: South Korea expects to reap a record tax windfall from the artificial intelligence-driven semiconductor boom, giving President Lee Jae Myung’s government fresh fiscal firepower to fund an ambitious investment agenda.

item.title: MUFG Surpasses Toyota to Become Japan’s Most Valuable Firm
item.description: Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group Inc.’s stock market value shot up to the highest in Japan, marking the first time a bank reached the top position since the current so-called three megabank groups were established.

item.title: Yen Falls on Report Japan Has No Plans to Change GPIF Allocation
item.description: The yen weakened and Japanese government bonds extended losses after Reuters reported that Japan has no plans to overhaul the Government Pension Investment Fund’s asset allocation.

item.title: France Unemployment to Hit Seven-Year High in 2026, Survey Shows
item.description: French unemployment is forecast to reach its highest level since 2019, raising fresh concerns over the fragility of the euro area’s second largest economy.

item.title: Euro-Area Outlook Cut by Economists as Iran War Weighs on Region
item.description: Growth in the euro zone is set to be weaker this year than previously predicted after hostilities in the Middle East resumed, economists say.

item.title: Healthcare Looks Ready to Star in Rotation Trade
item.description: A compelling argument is growing for healthcare stocks to be among the big winners in the rotation to more defensive parts of the market as the sector’s outlook improves.

item.title: Romanian Inflation Starts to Ease as Oil Still Casts Shadow
item.description: Romanian inflation eased as the impact of last year’s tax increases gradually faded away with the outlook for potential interest-rate cuts clouded by volatile oil prices.

item.title: Bridgepoint Buys Large Stake in Danish Drone Firm UMag Solutions
item.description: UK-listed private capital firm Bridgepoint Group is acquiring a majority stake in UMag Solutions ApS, a Danish defense technology company, adding to a raft of deals involving dronemakers.

item.title: Tata Capital Enters Red-Hot Gold Loan Market Through Acquisition
item.description: Tata Capital Ltd., one of India’s biggest shadow lenders, is entering the country’s $194 billion gold loan market by acquiring a majority stake in Yogakshemam Loans Ltd., intensifying competition in the nation’s fastest-growing lending segment.

item.title: Oil Stocks Rise, Tech Stocks Fall After Latest Iran Strikes
TSMC Sales Surge 36% in Fresh Sign of AI Spending Momentum
item.description: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. reported quarterly sales rose 36%, meeting high expectations and signaling global demand for AI hardware remains intact.

item.title: US and Iran Trade Fresh Strikes, Dispute Whether Hormuz Is Open
item.description: The US and Iran exchanged fresh strikes overnight into Monday as they continued their tit-for-tat attacks while issuing conflicting declarations over whether the Strait of Hormuz was open to shipping.

item.title: South Africa Plans First Strategic Oil Boost Since Apartheid
item.description: South Africa plans to increase its strategic oil reserves for the first time since the apartheid government stockpiled crude, adding to measures across the continent to mitigate supply shocks.

item.title: Global Funds Return to Indian Stocks With $1 Billion in Buying
item.description: Foreign investors poured more than $1 billion into Indian equities last week, with Goldman Sachs Group Inc. predicting further inflows as a stable currency and improved earnings expectations prompt funds to add to their holdings.

item.title: El Niño and Iran War Team Up in a Food Squeeze
item.description: US consumers are already on edge after prices never fell from post-Covid inflation.

item.title: Gold Bars, Cash Mark Fall of Indonesia’s Top Graft Hunter
item.description: Rows of gold bars, stacks of US and Singapore dollars and seven suitcases found inside a locked safe have become the defining images of one of the biggest scandals to hit Indonesia’s law-enforcement establishment in years.

item.title: MiniMax Shares Slump After JPMorgan Cuts Target Price Further
item.description: MiniMax Group Inc.’s shares plunged, after JPMorgan Chase & Co. slashed the Chinese AI model maker’s price target for the second time in less than a week on value dilution concerns caused by fresh fundraising.

item.title: China Expands Strategic Mineral Toolkit With New Investment Firm
item.description: A new, Beijing-backed mining investment vehicle is aimed at bolstering China’s grip on overseas resources, as the country pushes back against US and European efforts to curb its dominance of the mineral supply chain.

item.title: SBI Funds IPO Anchor Book Draws Capital Group, BlackRock, Goldman, GIC
item.description: The Capital Group Inc., BlackRock Inc., Fidelity Investments and Goldman Sachs Asset Management L.P. are among key investors that participated in the anchor book of SBI Funds Management Ltd., which was subscribed more than 20 times before the company’s initial public offering, according to people familiar with the matter.

item.title: Nippon Paint Offers $8.6 Billion for Akzo Nobel’s Paint Business
item.description: Nippon Paint Holdings Co. has made an offer for Akzo Nobel NV’s decorative paints business in the past month.

item.title: India Inflows at Risk With Foreigners’ Bearish Futures Bets, Mideast Flareup
item.description: Foreign funds’ bearish contracts remain close to last year’s record levels.

item.title: Hyundai Motor Workers Strike Over Bonuses, Robot Job Security
item.description: Hyundai Motor Co. workers began a three-day partial strike on Monday as their union demands bigger bonuses following landmark deals at semiconductor companies, and seek guarantees jobs won’t be lost to AI and robots.
